initiatives.name: Your Shares: Matched Employee Share Plan Launch
initiatives.summary: Rolls-Royce transitioned its all-employee share plan from Save As You Earn to a new global purchase plan where the company matches personal investment monthly, with 66% of eligible colleagues choosing to participate, aiming to drive engagement through share ownership.

evidence.title: Global employee share ownership plan launch (Your Shares: Matched)
evidence.summary: Rolls-Royce transitioned its all-employee share plan from Save As You Earn to a new global purchase plan where the company matches personal investment monthly, with 66% of eligible colleagues choosing to participate, aiming to drive engagement through share ownership.
evidence.quote: The all-employee share plan transitioned from a Save As You Earn plan, which was cash settled outside of the UK and share settled in the UK, and saw the launch of a global purchase plan (Your Shares: Matched), where the Company matches personal investment up to a certain value each month, allowing all colleagues to become shareholders. The Committee is pleased with the level of engagement with the new plan, with 66% of eligible colleagues choosing to participate.

initiatives.name: Commercial and Cost Optimisation Transformation
initiatives.summary: Rolls-Royce embedded a new commercial mindset and cost-conscious culture, adopting value-based pricing and renegotiating all original equipment contracts and onerous aftermarket contracts in Civil Aerospace, as part of the broader transformation programme.

evidence.title: Commercial and cost optimisation across all three divisions
evidence.summary: Rolls-Royce embedded a new commercial mindset and cost-conscious culture, adopting value-based pricing and renegotiating all original equipment contracts and onerous aftermarket contracts in Civil Aerospace, as part of the broader transformation programme.
evidence.quote: As part of our transformation, we have embedded a new commercial mindset and cost-conscious culture across the organisation. Commercial optimisation remains a key area of focus as we adopt a value-based pricing approach across the Group. This has been a significant driver of improved performance in all three divisions. For example, in Civil Aerospace where we are driving higher aftermarket margins, we have now renegotiated all our original equipment (OE) contracts.

initiatives.name: Shadow Carbon Price Investment Framework

evidence.quote: To help us meet our Scope 1 + 2 targets and make the right investment decisions we will be introducing a shadow carbon price as part of our investment decisions from 2026 onwards.

initiatives.name: Net Zero 2050 Commitment with 2030 Interim Targets
initiatives.summary: Rolls-Royce is committed to reaching net zero by end of 2050, with interim targets to reduce Scope 1+2 emissions by 46% by end of 2030 against a 2019 baseline, and ensuring all products are compatible with net zero operations by 2050.

evidence.title: Net zero by 2050 with interim 2030 emissions targets
evidence.summary: Rolls-Royce is committed to reaching net zero by end of 2050, with interim targets to reduce Scope 1+2 emissions by 46% by end of 2030 against a 2019 baseline, and ensuring all products are compatible with net zero operations by 2050.
evidence.quote: We are committed to reaching net zero by the end of 2050. We will measure our progress against the following interim and long-term targets: — reduce Scope 1 + 2 emissions by 46% by the end of 2030 against a 2019 baseline; — reduce Scope 1 + 2 emissions to net zero by the end of 2050;

evidence.quote: During the year, we created a new role on the Executive Team of Chief Procurement and Supply Chain Officer. It underscores our commitment to address these issues for the benefit of our customers and other stakeholders. I look forward to working with Martin Thomsen when he takes up this role in March.

initiatives.name: UltraFan Narrowbody Re-entry and Decarbonisation
initiatives.summary: Rolls-Royce is developing UltraFan technology for both widebody and narrowbody applications, building a narrowbody-sized demonstrator with up to 30,000 pounds of thrust, planned for ground testing in 2028, to re-enter the narrowbody market in partnership.

evidence.title: Re-entry into narrowbody aircraft engine market via UltraFan
evidence.summary: Rolls-Royce is developing UltraFan technology for both widebody and narrowbody applications, building a narrowbody-sized demonstrator with up to 30,000 pounds of thrust, planned for ground testing in 2028, to re-enter the narrowbody market in partnership.
evidence.quote: To progress this opportunity, we are building a narrowbody sized demonstrator with up to 30,000 pounds of thrust, which is planned for ground testing in 2028. We have already made significant investments in UltraFan and will continue to do so as we look to re-enter the narrowbody market in partnership.

evidence.title: UNIFIED project to decarbonise aviation with UltraFan demonstrator
evidence.summary: Rolls-Royce was selected by the EU's Clean Aviation programme to lead the UNIFIED project, involving industrial, academic and research partners across six European countries, enabling ground testing of an UltraFan technology demonstrator for future narrowbody aircraft.
evidence.quote: selected by the European Union's Clean Aviation programme to lead the Ultra Novel and Innovative Fully Integrated Engine Demonstrations (UNIFIED), one of 12 ground-breaking new projects aiming to decarbonise aviation. This project contains key industrial, academic and research partners across France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain and the UK.

initiatives.name: Power Systems Additive Manufacturing Optimisation
initiatives.summary: Power Systems redesigned, optimised, printed and tested highly stressed core components for the Series 2000 engine using additive manufacturing, producing lighter components with geometries impossible via traditional manufacturing, with potential to enable faster production of development, production, and spare parts across the portfolio.

evidence.title: Additive manufacturing breakthrough in Power Systems
evidence.summary: Power Systems redesigned, optimised, printed and tested highly stressed core components for the Series 2000 engine using additive manufacturing, producing lighter components with geometries impossible via traditional manufacturing, with potential to enable faster production of development, production, and spare parts across the portfolio.
evidence.quote: In an important breakthrough, Power Systems has redesigned, optimised, printed and tested numerous highly stressed core components in our Series 2000 engine. The team took advantage of the design freedom and new possibilities offered by the additive manufacturing techniques to deliver a lighter component, with geometries that could not be achieved with traditional manufacturing processes.
